prompt: Explain how U.S. health insurance works using only fantasy football metaphors.
response:
**U.S. Health Insurance, Explained Entirely in Fantasy Football Metaphors**

Imagine the entire U.S. healthcare system is one giant, year-round fantasy football league with 330 million players. Here’s how it actually works:

### 1. The League (The Insurance Market)
You can’t just play in any league you want. There are only a few big “platforms” that run leagues:
- Employer-sponsored leagues (the most popular, like being auto-drafted into your company’s keeper league)
- Obamacare/Federal Exchange leagues (the public waiver-wire leagues)
- Medicare leagues (the 65+ retirement league)
- Medicaid leagues (the income-based developmental league)

Each platform has its own scoring settings, buy-in costs, and rules.

### 2. The Buy-In (Premiums)
Every season you have to pay a **league fee** (your monthly premium). This money doesn’t go into a pot you can win back—it pays the commissioner, the servers, the injury analysts, and most importantly, it creates a giant **shared injury slush fund**.

You pay this fee *even if your team stays perfectly healthy all year*. That’s how the system works. Healthy teams subsidize the teams that get destroyed by injuries.

### 3. The Roster (Your Plan)
Your fantasy team has limited roster spots:
- **Deductible** = Your starting quarterback who has to get “activated” (you pay the first several thousand dollars yourself before the league starts covering your injured players).
- **Out-of-Pocket Maximum** = The salary cap on how much pain your team can possibly feel in one season. Once you hit this number, the league says “enough” and covers 100% the rest of the year.
- **Coinsurance/Co-pay** = Every time one of your players gets hurt, you still have to throw in a little bit of your own beer money (20% of the hospital bill, or $25 per doctor visit, etc.).

### 4. The Waiver Wire & Provider Networks
You can’t just pick up any injured player in the country. You’re locked into your league’s **provider network**—a specific group of doctors and hospitals that have agreed to be on your platform. 

Go to an “out-of-network” hospital? That’s like picking up a player from a rival fantasy platform. The league will either refuse to cover it or make you pay 2–3x as much.
